mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in CPIAUCSL above 3% for three consecutive months signals entrenched inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which reduces equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 3.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening labor demand, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST for two consecutive months signals a broad-based deterioration in aggregate demand, which depresses earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in INDPRO above 0.4% for six consecutive months signals robust supply growth, which typically coincides with higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 0.4% for six months is not followed by positive S&P 500 20-day returns in at least 70% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in FEDFUNDS above 4.5% in a single month signals an aggressive tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both GDPC1 and RSAFS above their 12-month moving averages signals a demand-led economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both exceed 12-month moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS above 0.5% for three consecutive months signals strong labor market momentum, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.3%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in FEDFUNDS below 1.0% for four consecutive months signals an extended easing cycle, which lowers borrowing costs and supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
